subject.name: G experiment trial 1, Arm A — salon weekly brief page
subject.surface: one page carrying a weekly money total for a salon owner, generated by an agent with no NodeKit, from figures the build produced rather than read

appliesWhenSatisfied: the surface presents a figure a user would act on — the weekly total is the product's entire output, and the trial rubric scored it as the owner's Monday answer
the data source is unbound, unconnected, or synthetic — the trial record states Arm A fabricated its data, and that neither arm was ever tested against a real Square export
zero is a plausible real value for this metric — a quiet week genuinely totals zero, so the reader has no internal contradiction to prompt a second look

doesNotApplyWhenChecked.clause: the metric is a genuine measured zero from a bound source — that must render, and suppressing it would be its own lie
doesNotApplyWhenChecked.note: Nothing is bound. There is no measurement here to suppress.

doesNotApplyWhenChecked.clause: the surface is a management or settings list with no metric to withhold (see obs-wise-empty's own boundary)
doesNotApplyWhenChecked.note: The metric is the whole surface; there is nothing else on the page.

doesNotApplyWhenChecked.clause: the figure is explicitly framed as an example inside disclosed demo mode
doesNotApplyWhenChecked.note: Contested, and scored as not firing. The page does mark the data in bold — 'This preview uses sample data, not your real numbers' — but there is no demo mode the reader entered or can leave, and the trial record places the marking below the fold. A framing the reader has to scroll to find is a caption, not a mode. This is the clause the human review returns to.

rejectedSubjects.name: NodeRoom create-room dialog — 'How should NodeAgent edits land?', review-every-artifact-edit as recommended default against auto-approve
rejectedSubjects.excludedByClause: the surface is a management or settings list with no metric to withhold (see obs-wise-empty's own boundary)
rejectedSubjects.note: Considered first and put down. The dialog presents a governance choice, not a metric: it renders no figure, has no data source to be unbound from, and zero is not a value it could display. Every appliesWhen condition of rule-absence-is-not-zero fails on it. Scoring it against this rule would have produced real fact ids attached to a subject the rule does not govern, which is the failure mode the corpus exists to prevent. The dialog is a trust surface and belongs to a different rule that this collection has not yet derived.

anchors.0: renders the numeral with nothing on the surface distinguishing it from a measurement — obs-midday-empty's two metric tiles
anchors.1: renders the numeral; a distinguishing statement exists on the surface but not within reach of the figure
anchors.2: renders the numeral; a distinguishing statement is placed at the figure
anchors.3: withholds the numeral and states the absence, but offers no action that would bind a source
anchors.4: withholds the numeral, states the absence naming the object that is missing, and offers exactly one binding action — obs-quicken-empty

criteria.question: Does the surface withhold the numeral while its data source is unbound?

citations.note: Quicken displays zero numerals in the content area while unbound. Arm A displays a weekly total in the typography of a measurement.
Wise also displays zero numerals while unbound, on a second product, which is what makes the bar a bar rather than one company's habit.

Midday's secondary tiles render a numeral while unbound, typeset identically to a measured value. Arm A does the same thing with a nonzero figure, which is the more legible form of the same error: $0 at least stays inside the range of true answers.

criteria.finding: The page renders synthetic weekly money as a figure. This is the rule's core prohibition and the subject fails it outright.

criteria.question: Is there any statement on the surface distinguishing the rendered figure from a measured one?

citations.note: Midday's tiles carry zero words distinguishing zero from absent — no marker, tooltip, or caption. Arm A carries the statement in bold, so on this criterion alone it is above the shipped counterexample. This is the one place the subject beats a real product.

criteria.finding: Present and set in bold: 'This preview uses sample data, not your real numbers.' Short of 4 only because the rule asks for refusal rather than annotation.

criteria.question: Is the distinguishing statement reachable from the figure without the reader going looking for it?

citations.note: Midday attaches its qualifying text to an affordance adjacent to the figure itself. Arm A's statement sits below the fold. Flagged false: obs-midday-bound/f1 is not among rule-absence-is-not-zero's derivedFrom.factIds, so this criterion is reaching past the rule's own evidence.

criteria.finding: Below the fold. Under the rule's mechanism — the eye reaches the figure before the caption — a statement the reader must scroll to is a statement the reader reaches second.

criteria.question: Does the statement name the object that is missing, in the user's terms rather than the system's?

citations.note: Quicken names the object: 'No holdings to display.' Arm A names it too — 'not your real numbers' — so the missing thing is identified rather than described as a system state.

Wise makes the user the grammatical subject: 'You don't have any bank accounts connected.' Arm A's subject is 'This preview' — the artifact talking about itself. Flagged false: obs-wise-empty/f2 is not in the rule's derivedFrom.factIds.

criteria.finding: Names the missing object but not the user's situation. Half the positive pattern.

criteria.question: Is an action offered that would bind a real source, and is it the only action?

citations.note: Quicken pairs the absence statement with one uncontested control, 'CONNECT ACCOUNT'. Arm A offers no binding action at all: there is nothing to click that would replace the figure with a measured one. Flagged false: obs-quicken-empty/f3 is not in the rule's derivedFrom.factIds.

criteria.finding: None. The page tells the reader the numbers are not hers and then offers her no way to make them hers, which leaves the disclosure as a dead end.

criteria.question: Does the surface say how its own figure can be misread, at the figure?

citations.note: Midday names the specific misreading its own figure invites — 'if the revenue appears too high, internal transfers may have been marked as income' — and does it on a figure that is genuinely bound. Arm A says only that the source is sample data. It never says what a reader who acts on the figure would get wrong.

criteria.finding: Discloses the provenance, not the consequence. A bound figure in the corpus does more disclosure work than this unbound one, which is the comparison that makes the gap legible.

scoreBasis: The scale is a ladder, not an average: the subject sits at the highest anchor it satisfies. c1 places it in the render-the-numeral half, so anchors 3 and 4 are closed. c2 lifts it off anchor 0 — a distinguishing statement exists. c3 holds it at anchor 1 rather than 2, because the statement is not placed at the figure. c4, c5 and c6 are recorded because they are what the surface would have to fix to climb, and because c5's zero is the reason the disclosure leads nowhere; none of them can move a subject that is already blocked at c1.

humanReview.reason: The citation, not the reading. c3 is the only criterion separating anchor 1 from anchor 2, and its sole support is obs-midday-bound/f1 — which is not in rule-absence-is-not-zero's derivedFrom.factIds, and which is an observation of a bound figure disclosing its own definition. obs-midday-bound's recorded tension says that axis is 'a distinct axis from whether the data is real'. So the adjacency standard that costs this surface a point was imported from a fact the rule does not stand on, applied to a question the fact was not observed answering. Under the rule's own six facts, the record supports 'a distinguishing statement is present and marked' and does not reach placement. That is anchor 2. Noting what this does not do: it does not touch c1. The surface still renders fabricated money as a figure, and the difference between 2 and 4 is the whole finding. The disagreement is over one point and one citation, and it is on the record so the next reader can take the other side.

notScored: Arm B of the same trial. Its surface has no disclosure anywhere in the product and would score 0 on this ladder, but the trial record documents it in far more detail than Arm A, and a receipt is more useful on the borderline case than on the obvious one.
Whether the figure changes after a real Square export is connected. Arm A's parser would break on a quoted comma per the trial record, so the bound state was never reached and cannot be scored.
Everything the rule does not govern: the software claims, the missing artifacts under Arm A's 'Verified' heading, cost, and file count. Those are scored by the trial rubric, not by this rule.
Motion. rule-absence-is-not-zero is a static rule and this collection holds no timing, easing or choreography facts to cite.
boundary: Scored from a dated first-party record, not from the running page — the Arm A tree is outside this repository, so no locator here was re-derived by inspection. Every claim about the subject traces to evolution/artifacts/g-experiment-trial-1.md and inherits that document's own limits, including its author's disclosed methodology errors. A re-inspection could move c2, c3 and c4; it cannot move c1, which the record states in bold.
